jurisdiction.name: San Marino
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: San Marino has no AI-specific law, strategy or guidance. Its AI governance rests on the GDPR-style data protection law (Law 171/2018), which regulates automated decision-making, and on a January 2024 resolution of the Great and General Council committing the Government to regulate AI along the lines of the EU AI Act; by late 2024 the Government reported the matter was still under study. San Marino is a party to the Council of Europe's data protection convention (Convention 108).
lead_institutions: Autorità Garante per la protezione dei dati personali
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 13 October 2026 from the Great and General Council's website and the data protection authority's website. The official bulletin's own search could not be used, so the gazette was covered through Council documents. The Government's follow-up on AI regulation is tracked as a lead.

instruments.official_title: Legge 21 dicembre 2018 n.171 - Protezione delle persone fisiche con riguardo al trattamento dei dati personali
instruments.english_title: Law No. 171 of 21 December 2018 on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data
instruments.issuing_authority: Great and General Council (promulgated by the Captains Regent)
instruments.current_status: In force. Art. 129 provides entry into force on the fifteenth day after legal publication; the legal publication date is not printed in the text, so no effective date is recorded. Articles 52 and 58 (the Data Protection Authority's establishment, composition and tasks) were revised by Delegated Decree No. 84 of 30 April 2021, ratified by Delegated Decree No. 138 of 19 July 2021. Supervised by the Autorità Garante per la protezione dei dati personali.
instruments.summary: San Marino's general data protection law, modelled on the EU GDPR and applying to wholly or partly automated processing of personal data by controllers established in San Marino. Art. 22 gives data subjects the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produces legal or similarly significant effects, with exceptions for contracts and explicit consent subject to safeguards including human intervention; arts. 13-14 require meaningful information about the logic involved in automated decision-making. It establishes the Autorità Garante per la protezione dei dati personali as the supervisory authority.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Governs personal-data processing used to train and run AI systems, including automated decision-making and profiling (art. 22).

instruments.official_title: Delibera n.15 del Consiglio Grande e Generale del 17 gennaio 2024 - Istanza d'Arengo affinchè sia regolamentato il settore informatico dell'Intelligenza Artificiale (Istanza n.13 dell'8 ottobre 2023)
instruments.english_title: Resolution No. 15 of the Great and General Council of 17 January 2024 approving the Arengo petition for regulation of the artificial intelligence sector (Petition No. 13 of 8 October 2023)
instruments.current_status: Adopted with 25 votes in favour on 17 January 2024. On 2 December 2024 the Secretary of State for Education and Culture reported to the First Permanent Council Committee (under art. 7(2) of Law No. 72 of 24 May 1995) that the Government was still studying AI regulation with the University of San Marino; no AI law or decree had been found as of 2026-10-13.
instruments.summary: The Great and General Council approved a citizens' Istanza d'Arengo asking that the AI sector be regulated within the parameters of the EU's proposed AI Regulation. The resolution commits the Congress of State (the Government) to take the consequent measures within its competences and, under art. 7 of Law No. 72 of 24 May 1995, to report them to the competent Permanent Council Committee within six months. It is the only parliamentary act found that directs the Government to regulate AI.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Parliamentary mandate to the Government to regulate AI along the lines of the EU AI Act.
